answer: A farm that parks keys in the jury pool thus watches its influence decay while paying the river fee to keep them eligible. Because the wharf decay is applied at each close, the prism audit makes public the reduced weight and the seat has to be earned again. A juror that skips cases loses 13% of its weight per missed epoch, so sitting on a seat without doing the work is not a passive strategy. A 215 account operation therefore ties up 1 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
